hinge.title: Use front, top, and side views to represent or identify a solid when a single projection is not enough.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: single projection still holds here even though Use three views when matching or reconstructing a solid from plane drawings because one is missing from the stem — on the item about Use front, top, and side views to represent or identify.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Stronger representation of the solid is what produces multiple perpendicular projections from named directions, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Use front, top, and side views to represent or identify.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The single projection rule also covers this: {'excluded_case': 'Do not identify a solid from only one projection when the task supplies three views.', so it is not an exception — on the item about Use front, top, and side views to represent or identify.

intelligence.enrichment: A single projection is not made by a unique object, so three mutually perpendicular projections are often used: the vertical-plane projection is the front view, the horizontal-plane projection is the top view, and the side-plane projection is the side view.
